text: . Prime Minister Narendra Modi has extended his greetings to the citizens on the occasion of Ayurveda Day today. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that Ayurveda is not merely a method of treatment but a powerful means of a healthy and balanced lifestyle. The Prime Minister called upon people to resolve to embrace this rich heritage more firmly.AYUSH Minister Prataprao Jadhav also extended greetings to all the citizens, Ayurvedic physicians, and vaidyas on the occasion of Ayurveda Day. In a social media post, Mr Jadhav called upon the citizens to embrace country’s ancient medical system and build a healthy, prosperous, and self-reliant India.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh today held a discussion with the European Parliament delegation focusing on effective implementation of India-EU FTA. The delegation,comprisingmembers of the European Parliament’s Committee on Industry, Research and Energy, met Dr Singh in New Delhi. During the meeting, both sides discussed deepening cooperation in Science, Technology and Emerging Technologies.On the occasion, Dr Singh said the India-EU strategic partnership offers significant opportunities for closer collaboration in areas of mutual priority, with science and research forming an integral part of the partnership. He added that the FTA will open new opportunities for businesses, consumers and skilled professionals and provide further momentum to the multifaceted India-EU strategic partnership.Member of European Parliament Angelika Winzig said that India is a key strategic partner for the European Union. She said the delegation’s visit was aimed at gaining a deeper understanding of India’s industrial and technology policies and identifying areas for closer cooperation.

. India narrowly avoided a historic upset, defeating hosts Japan by two runs in a rain-curtailed, five-overs-a-side one-off T20 International match at the Sano International Cricket Ground today. This was India’s 200th victory in T20 Internationals, including Super Over wins. After a nearly 2.5-hour delay due to a wet outfield, India skipper Shreyas Iyer won the toss and opted to bat first. However, Japan’s spinners made the most of the conditions, restricting the visitors to 32 for 4 after five overs. Chasing 33 off 30 balls, Japan gave India a major scare and came agonisingly close to pulling off one of the biggest upsets in their cricketing history. Washington Sundar struck twice to halt Japan’s momentum, while Axar Patel kept things tight with his experience and control. The hosts managed to score 30 for 3 in five overs and eventually fell two runs short, handing India a nervy victory.

. Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana today.The weather agency has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Sikkim, Bihar, Jharkhand, Interior Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Konkan, Goa, Maharashtra and West Bengal.Thunderstorm accompanied with lightning may prevail over Madhya Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura and Rayalaseema today.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated the Women’s Cricket Team on winning the Gold medal at the Asian Games 2026, being held in Nagoya, Japan. Calling it a splendid triumph for Indian cricket, Mr Modi said that this victory also brings India its first Gold of this edition of the Games. In a social media post, he said that it was a commanding performance marked by confidence, skill, and wonderful teamwork. The Prime Minister said that the team has made the nation proud and will inspire countless young cricketers across the country.Prime Minister Modi also congratulated Suchika Tariyal on winning a Bronze medal in Mixed Martial Arts at the Asian Games. In a social media post, Mr Modi noted that she has secured India’s first-ever Asian Games medal in this field.PrimeMinister stated that her achievement is especially significant, highlighting her dedication and zeal, and extended his best wishes for many more successes ahead.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. US President Donald Trump has said his administration strongly supports the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor. He said there is a need to shift Middle East energy infrastructure away from Iranian checkpoints amid multiple strikes on West Asian countries during the war.President Trump made the remarks while addressing a meeting with Gulf Cooperation Council and Arab leaders on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York yesterday. President Trump said attacks on commercial shipping in neighbouring countries had highlighted the need to shift the region’s energy infrastructure. He said the region was close to overcoming longstanding challenges that have plagued this region for decades.The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), unveiled in 2023, comprises an Eastern Corridor connecting India to the Gulf region and a Northern Corridor connecting the Gulf region to Europe. It will include a railway and ship-rail transit network, as well as road transport routes.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has paid tributes to the National Poet Ramdhari Singh Dinkar on his birth anniversary today. In a social media post, the Prime Minister said that Mr Dinkar’s fiery poems, brimming with the sentiments of public awakening and national pride, continue to infuse valour, vigour and self-respect into the hearts of the countrymen even today.Mr Modi added that his works not only enrich literature but also inspire devotion to the motherland. The Prime Minister said that Mr Dinkar’s towering personality and timeless creations will guide generations of Indians for ages to come.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also paid tributes to the National Poet Ramdhari Singh Dinkar. In a social media post, the Lok Sabha Speaker said, in the firmament of Hindi literature, Mr Dinkar’s place is not merely as a great poet but as a litterateur whose pen gave voice to the nation’s consciousness, public sentiments, and social concerns.Mr Birla said that Dinkar’s timeless works, including Rashmirathi, Kurukshetra, Urvashi, Renuka and Four Chapters of Indian Culture have enriched Hindi literature and offered a fresh perspective on Indian society and national thought. He added that Mr Dinkar’s immortal literary legacy will continue to inspire Indian literature and national reflection.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said that integrated commerce and industry offices are being envisioned in major cities to provide businesses with a common point of access to multiple government departments and agencies. He made the announcement at a stakeholder workshop organised by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade in New Delhi yesterday. Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada also attended the programme.Mr. Goyal said the government is working to strengthen export facilitation through both physical and digital mechanisms. He said, instead of setting up separate offices of different departments at various locations, integrated offices will help businesses access multiple services at a single point.The Minister also announced the development of a digital platform, Trade Connect, which will provide exporters with product-wise and HSN-code-wise information. This will include tariffs in destination countries, Free Trade Agreement opportunities and procedures for availing FTA benefits.Mr. Goyal said the platform will use digital and AI-enabled tools to help businesses identify potential export opportunities and address infrastructure gaps.The workshop brought together representatives of industry associations, trade bodies and sectoral organisations. Discussions focused on Ease of Doing Business reforms, trade facilitation, opportunities arising from India’s Free Trade Agreements, and challenges faced by industry in accessing markets and navigating regulatory procedures.

. India defeated Bangladesh 3-nil, without dropping a single game across three matches, to reach the Men’s Badminton team quarter-finals at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium in Japan today. Lakshya Sen beat Jaman Ayman Ibn, followed by Ayush Shetty’s win over Gourab Singha. Kidambi Srikanth then sealed the tie with a victory over Jumar Al-Amin.Paris 2024 semi-finalist Lakshya comfortably beat Ayman Ibn 21-4, 21-12 to give India a 1-nil lead. Ayush registered a convincing 21-4, 21-13 win over Singha to stretch the lead to 2-nil, before Srikanth sealed the tie with a 21-15, 21-9 victory over Jumar Al-Amin.India will face hosts Japan in the quarter-finals tomorrow, with a win in the tie guaranteeing the team a medal.The Indian women’s team will also face Japan in the quarter-finals tomorrow after beating Kazakhstan 3-nil in its opening tie yesterday.

The inaugural ceremony of 11th Ayurveda Day, based on the theme “  Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow,” will be held at the Kavivarya Suresh Bhat Auditorium in Nagpur from 9 to 10 AM this morning.Vice-Chancellor of the National Institute of Ayurveda, Jaipur, Dr. Sanjeev Sharma, informing about this event, said that this year’s Ayurveda Day will focus on strengthening Ayurveda through evidence, research and innovation, while promoting community health and well-being.Director of the Institute of Liver and Biliary Sciences, Delhi, Dr. Shiv Kumar Sarin, will address a scientific session on “Integrating Therapies is needed to reduce NCD (Non-Communicable Diseases) Burden by 2027”. Subsequently, Dr. Geeta Krishnan Pillai, Unit Head of the Global Traditional Medicine Centre, Jamnagar, will speak on “Shashwatam to Vishwas – Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow and the Road to 2047”The programme will also witness the launch of “From Traditional Wisdom to Global Leadership: Ayush Vision 2030” Report, the Status Report on Ayush-related Inventions in India, and the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences – Ayurveda Gyan Naipunya Initiative)CCRAS-AGNI an Assessment Scale Web Portal.Ayurveda institutions, practitioners and various stakeholders from across the country and the world will participate in the   11th Ayurveda Day celebrations. Dhananjay Wankhede, Akashvani News, Nagpur.

The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. The Indian Women’s Cricket team reasserted its continental dominance by clinching a second successive gold medal at the Asian Games, thrashing Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final at Nisshin in Japan today. Opting to bat, India posted 216 for the loss of three wickets in the stipulated 20 overs, the highest total in Asian Games history, riding on Smriti Mandhana’s 79 runs off 45 balls and Richa Ghosh’s 48 off 22. In reply, Sri Lanka were bowled out for just 69 in 15.4 overs. This is India’s first gold medal at the ongoing Asiad and overall seventh medal.Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the Women’s Cricket Team on the feat. Calling it a splendid triumph for Indian cricket, Mr Modi said that this victory also brings India its first Gold of this edition of the Games. In a social media post, he said that it was a commanding performance marked by confidence, skill, and wonderful teamwork. The Prime Minister said that the team has made the nation proud and will inspire countless young cricketers across the country.Indian men’s Badminton team defeated hosts Japan in the quarterfinals and assured itself of a medal at the Asian Games. Lakshya Sen was staring at defeat after losing the opening game and trailing 14-19 in the decider. However, Lakshya made a comeback, reeling off seven straight points to beat world No.7 and two-time world championships silver-medallist Kodai Naraoka 11-21, 21-5, 21-19 to give India a 1-0 lead. Playing the first doubles, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, who have won two titles this season, registered a 21-18, 24-22 win over former world champions Hoki Takuro and Kobayashi Yugo to extend India’s lead to 2-0. Ayush Shetty then produced an impressive performance to see off world no. 16 Koki Watanabe 21-10 21-19 to seal the match and a medal for India.  The Indian men were the silver-medallists of the last edition.In Wushu, India’s Roshibina Devi also confirmed a medal at the Asian Games after securing a 5-0 win over Chu Man Sin of Macao, in the Women’s 60kg quarterfinals. Roshibina, the 2018 and 2022 Asiad medallist, has now secured a third continental medal with another strong performance to advance to the semifinals. Roshibina will now be in action in the semifinals tomorrow for a place in the final. She is already a silver medallist from the 2023 Asian Games, when she came second in theSanda60 kg category. She also bagged a bronze medal in the 2018 Jakarta Games in the same weight category.Apart from her, India’s Aryan also moved to the quarterfinals as he fights for a medal. Aryan defeated Afghanistan’s Safi Shahzada in the Men’s 56kg pre-quarters 2-0 to progress into the quarterfinals.Indian boxer Jadumani Singh defeated Nepal’s Chandra Bahadur Thapa to march into the pre-quarters in the Men’s 55kg preliminary round at the Nishio Gymnasium in Japan today. Commonwealth Games silver medallist Jadumani registered a unanimous 5-0 win over the reigning World Championships’ bronze medallist Thapa with a brilliant bout. Jadumani will now be up against Filipino boxer Carlo Paalam in the pre-quarters on Saturday. Paalam is a silver medallist from the 2020 Tokyo Olympic Games.Earlier, Glasgow Games gold medallist Sakshi Chaudhary defeated Paris Olympics bronze medallist Aira Villegas in the preliminary round at the Asian Games 2026 to march into the pre-quarters. Sakshi outclassed the Filipino pugilist by a unanimous decision of 5-0. She will be facing current 51kg world champion Alua Balkibekova on Thursday.In Men’s Cricket, India narrowly avoided a historic upset, defeating hosts Japan by two runs in a rain-curtailed, five-overs-a-side one-off T20 International match at the Sano International Cricket Ground today. This was India’s 200th victory in T20 Internationals, including Super Over wins. After a nearly 2.5-hour delay due to a wet outfield, India skipper Shreyas Iyer won the toss and opted to bat first. However, Japan’s spinners made the most of the conditions, restricting the visitors to 32 for 4 after five overs. Chasing 33 off 30 balls, Japan gave India a major scare and came agonisingly close to pulling off one of the biggest upsets in their cricketing history. Washington Sundar struck twice to halt Japan’s momentum, while Axar Patel kept things tight with his experience and control. The hosts managed to score 30 for 3 in five overs and eventually fell two runs short, handing India a nervy victory.

The Reserve Bank of India has extended an existing KYC facility available to Non-Resident Indians and Persons of Indian Origin to Foreign Portfolio Investors, allowing banks to accept original certified copies of KYC documents certified by specified authorities abroad.Under the amended directions, banks may accept an original certified copy of Aadhaar-related proof or an officially valid document for FPIs, with the certification done by specified authorities. The certified copies may be attested by authorised officials of overseas branches of Scheduled Commercial Banks registered in India, branches of overseas banks having relationships with Indian banks, Notary Public abroad, Court Magistrate, Judge, or the Indian Embassy/Consulate General in the country where the non-resident customer resides.The amendment was issued on Friday through the RBI (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026 and came into effect immediately.

. Ayushman Bharat – the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana has completed eight years today. Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched this scheme in September 2018 from Ranchi, Jharkhand, which has become the world’s largest government-funded health assurance scheme.Prime Minister Modi said that the scheme has enabled record savings on medical expenses and benefited the poor and middle class. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that eight years ago, Ayushman Bharat was rolled out with the idea that every Indian should have access to top-quality and affordable healthcare. He said, today, more than 60 crore beneficiaries have access to five lakh annual health cover, making it the largest healthcare scheme in the world. The Prime Minister said, Ayushman Arogya Mandirs have already recorded over 500 crore visits, strengthening primary healthcare at the grassroots.Our correspondent reports that more than 48 crore 54 lakh Ayushman cards have been created so far. Over the past eight years, around 13 crore beneficiaries have availed cashless treatment, and the government has spent more than two lakh crore rupees on it.Under the scheme, a total of 38 thousand government and private hospitals have been empanelled. The scheme is now being implemented across all 36 States and Union Territories, marking a significant milestone in expanding healthcare access and strengthening the delivery of secondary and tertiary care services across the country.Recently, the Modi government has extended the benefits of this scheme to senior citizens of 70 years and 37 lakh families of ASHAs and anganwadi workers. The main aim of the scheme is to provide universal health care to the poor, needy and vulnerable sections of the country.Union Health and Family Welfare Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda today said that the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana scheme has transformed healthcare access for millions across the country.On the 8th anniversary of the scheme, Mr Nadda said that the scheme is turning the promise of quality healthcare and financial protection into a reality for families across the country. Nadda also said that the scheme is covering more than half a billion people across the country.In a social media post, he emphasised that the world’s largest Health Assurance Scheme has covered more than sixty crore people. The Minister further said that guided by the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Government remains steadfast in its commitment to strengthen an accessible, affordable and inclusive healthcare system. He added that the Government is also ensuring that every citizen can access quality healthcare with dignity and without financial hardship.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. India won three medals in shooting at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, today.In the men’s 10-meter air rifle individual event, Himanshu Dhillon won the silver medal, while Rudrankksh Patil secured the bronze. India also bagged a silver medal in the men’s team event of the same competition.Yesterday, Elavenil Valarivan won the silver medal in the women’s individual 10-metre air rifle event. India also bagged a silver medal in the women’s team event of the same competition. With this, India has won a total of five medals in Shooting so far, including four silver and one bronze.Suchika Tariyal has become the first athlete from the country to win a medal in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA). Suchika secured the bronze medal in the 60 kg category.In the medal tally, India is currently in 12th place with a total of six medals, including four silver and two bronze.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil, Himanshu Dhillon, and Parth Rakesh Mane on winning the silver medal in the Men’s 10 meter Air Rifle Team event at the Asian Games. In a social media post, Mr. Modi commended the trio, stating that their focus, consistency, and exceptional teamwork have made the entire nation proud.In addition to the team success, the Prime Minister lauded the athletes for their individual achievements in the Men’s 10 meter Air Rifle event. Congratulating Himanshu Dhillon on winning the silver medal, Mr Modi praised his composure and remarkable accuracy under pressure, noting that his performance was a source of national pride.Extending his congratulations to Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil for securing the bronze medal, Mr Modi appreciated his focus and discipline throughout the competition, wishing him continued success in all his future endeavors.

. India and New Zealand Free Trade Agreement will come into force from 20th of October this year. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said that the Agreement provides duty-free access for 100 per cent of Indian exports to New Zealand. He said, the strategic partnerships reflects the shared ambition to deepen this cooperation and aspirational goal of doubling bilateral trade in goods and services to almost 35 thousand crore rupees in the next 4 to 5 years.This will open new opportunities for Indian exports including textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, engineering goods, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and processed food products. At the same time, New Zealand will gain enhanced and access to the Indian market for products including wood, wool, sheep meat, and raw leather hides. The Agreement also creates new opportunities in services, investment and professional, student and youth mobility, including enhanced pathways for Indian professionals and students.It provides for facilitating 20 billion US dollars of investment into India and strengthens bilateral cooperation in areas including agricultural productivity, pharmaceuticals and medical devices, traditional medicine and AYUSH, technology and trade facilitation. India and New Zealand share longstanding and close relations, anchored in strong people-to-people ties and expanding cooperation across trade and investment, agriculture, education, sports, technology and other areas. The FTA represents a significant step in further strengthening these ties and creating new opportunities for businesses and communities in both countries.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has called for greater cooperation among Global South countries to address rising geopolitical tensions, economic challenges, climate shocks and pressures on the multilateral system.The Minister was addressing the meeting of Global South Countries on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York yesterday. Dr Jaishankar said the global situation was marked by increasing conflicts, pressure on supply chains and trade, fragmented investment flows, growing debt vulnerabilities and inadequate development finance. He said Global South countries should work together to address key challenges, including supply chain, finance and connectivity bottlenecks.The External Affairs Minister called for efforts to prevent the manipulation of energy availability and prices, ensure food security by addressing challenges related to grain and fertiliser supplies, and promote fair economic and trade practices. He also highlighted the need to enhance industrialisation and production capabilities, secure maritime commons, and ensure the safety and security of seafarers and commercial shipping.The External Affairs Minister further stressed the importance of managing the transformations brought by Artificial Intelligence to prevent divisions and called for greater inclusion in decision-making structures on issues affecting Global South countries.Dr Jaishankar also met Italy’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly. In a social media post, the Minister said their discussions focused on the Gulf situation, the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), and the Ukraine conflict. He said the two countries aimed to expand collaboration and increase trade ties.Addressing the India-CELAC Foreign Ministers’ Meeting during the UN High-Level Week 2026 in New York, the External Affairs Minister called for stronger economic and development partnerships between India and the Community of Latin American and Caribbean States (CELAC). He said, India-CELAC trade has now crossed 50 billion US dollars annually.Dr Jaishankar said, India emerged as one of the world’s major economies over the past decade, with its GDP more than doubling and growth remaining robust. He added that India today combines a large and increasingly skilled human resource base with increasing capabilities, a growing market, strong digital infrastructure and expanding technology capacities. He said India’s engagement with the Global South went beyond its national interest and reflected its commitment to shared prosperity.Highlighting India’s development cooperation with the region, Dr Jaishankar said India has placed its capabilities at the service of those in need. He cited projects supporting livelihoods in the Caribbean, assistance after Hurricane Melissa, military hospitals sent to Venezuela after the earthquake, and medicines supplied to Latin American countries. He said India and CELAC have complementary strengths.India brings technology, pharmaceuticals, skilled manpower and digital capabilities, while CELAC offers opportunities in critical minerals, sustainable energy, agriculture and food resources. Dr Jaishankar also said India and CELAC should consider upgrading the Annual Business Summit from next year.

. In Women’s cricket, India thrashed Sri Lanka to win first ever gold medal in the final in Asian Games 2026 at the Aichi Prefectural Korogi Sports Park, Japan. Sri Lanka were bowled out for just 69 in 15.4 overs, as India completed a comprehensive victory by 147 runs.Batting first, India posted a commanding 216 for 3 in 20 overs. Smriti Mandhana top-scored with 79 runs, while Richa Ghosh remained unbeaten on 49. Mandhana also became the first woman cricketer to complete 11,000 international runs during the innings.

. At the Asian Games, the Indian trio of Maheshwari Singh, Parinaaz Dhaliwal and Raiza Dhillon secured the bronze medal in the women’s team skeet shooting event at Aichi-Nagoya, taking country’s overall medal tally on Day 4 to eight.In another feat, Jay Meena made history in soft tennis, assuring country its first-ever medal in the sport. Jay has advanced to the semifinals, defeating Sherwin Nuguit of the Philippines 4-3 in a closely fought quarterfinal.In shooting, Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker has qualified for the final of women’s 10-metre air pistol event. She finished third in the qualification round. However, the trio of Manu, Suruchi Singh and Esha Singh failed to qualify in the team event.Indian swimmer Beniston Benedicton has qualified for the final of the men’s 100-metre butterfly event. He finished ninth overall in the heats to secure his place in the final which will be held at 1:38 PM today.In rowing at the Asian Games, Balraj Panwar has qualified for the final of the men’s singles sculls event. He finished third in his heat with a timing of 6 minutes 52.84 seconds and was fourth overall across the two heats. The final will be held tomorrow. India have also secured final berth in the men’s double sculls event. Satnam Singh and Salman Khan finished second in their heat, clocking 6 minutes 15.63 seconds. They finished fourth overall across the two heats and advanced to the final.In canoeing, the Indian Men’s Kayak Four team has qualified for the Final A. The Indian team finished third in the heats, clocking 1 minute 29.447 seconds to secure a place in the final.In Sepaktakraw, Indian Men’s Regu team defeated Philippines, 2-0 in the opening Group B match, registering 15-7, 15-10 win.Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu will take part in the women’s 49-kilogram final. The match is scheduled to begin at 10 AM. She will be aiming for her first Asian Games medal after finishing fourth at the Hangzhou Games in 2023.India is already assured of medals in Men’s badminton and Women’s Wushu. The Men’s badminton team will take on China in the semi-final today, after defeating Japan in the quarter-final yesterday. The match is scheduled to begin at 11:30 AM. In Wushu, Roshibina Devi will face Indonesia’s Thania Kusumaningtyas in the women’s 60-kilogram Sanda semi-final at 2:50 PM.India’s skeet shooters Anantjeet Singh Naruka, Bhavtegh Singh Gill and Mairaj Ahmad Khan will be in action on the final day of qualification.In Hockey, the Indian Women’s Team will face Thailand in their third Pool B match this morning. The match will begin 11:30 AM.Indian Men’s and Women’s kabaddi teams will also continue their group-stage campaigns.Yesterday, the Indian women’s cricket team clinched country’s first gold medal of the Games, defeating Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final. The victory took India’s medal tally to seven.In Boxing, Jadumani Singh advanced to the pre-quarterfinals in the Men’s 55-kilogram category, while Sakshi Chaudhary also progressed to the pre-quarterfinals.Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya has congratulated Parinaaz Dhaliwal, Raiza Dhillon and Maheshwari Chauhan on securing the first-ever Bronze Medal in the Women’s Skeet Team event at the Asian Games.Mr Mandaviya also extended wishes to Anantjeet Singh Naruka, Bhavtegh Singh Gill and Mairaj Ahmad Khan on securing the Bronze Medal in the Men’s Skeet Team.

. Google has been fined 403 million euros by Ireland’s Data Protection Commission for breaking strict European Union privacy rules regarding how it tracks people. Regulators found that between 2018 and 2020, Google unlawfully tracked and processed users’ location information through three main features, its Web & App Activity settings, its Location History mapping tool, and the Location Accuracy feature built into the Android operating system.Ireland is the lead regulator for Google in the 27-nation European Union because the US tech giant’s European headquarters is based in Dublin. The Irish watchdog takes the lead on these cases, and this six-year investigation concluded that Google failed to be open, fair, and transparent about how it handles this sensitive data.While this is the fourth-largest privacy fine the Irish regulator has ever handed out-behind even bigger penalties given to tech giants like Meta and TikTok, Google’s legal troubles in Europe are far from over, as the watchdog is still actively investigating three other privacy cases involving the company.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service. His journey is guided by the principle of “Jan Seva Se Desh Seva” and a continued commitment to public service. Inspired by this vision of service and good governance, the government is working towards the goal of a developed India by 2047. This commitment, through inclusive development and social empowerment, is bringing about a transformation in people’s lives. In this context, the PM-KISAN scheme has added new achievements to the lives of farmers across the country.In Madhya Pradesh, a large number of farmers are benefiting from the PM-KISAN scheme. Under the scheme, eligible farmers receive financial assistance of Rs 6,000 every year in three equal installments, directly into their bank accounts. This support is useful for farmers to meet their needs for fertilisers, seeds and other farming activities. The scheme was started in 2019. So far, more than Rs 4.47 lakh crore have been transferred to farmers through 23 installments. More than nine crore 49 lakh farmers benefited from the 23rd installment.The Central Government has now approved the continuation of the PM-KISAN scheme from 2026-27 to 2030-31. A total financial provision of Rs 3.15 crore has been made for the scheme. Chhindwara farmer Basant Patel said that farmers are happy with the decision to continue the scheme for five more years. Women farmers have also benefited from the scheme. More than Rs 1.6 lakh crore has been given to women farmers so far. The scheme uses digital verification, Aadhaar authentication and Direct Benefit Transfer to send the money directly to farmers.

. India’s women’s opener Smriti Mandhana has created history, as she has become the first cricketer in the world to score 11,000 runs in women’s international cricket. Smriti made this record during the Asian Games final against Sri Lanka at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin. Mandhana smashed three sixes and three fours in the first four overs to get India off to a blistering start. She surpassed former Indian captain Mithali Raj’s record of 10,868 runs.

. Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare Anupriya Patel today said that India’s journey in Pharmacovigilance has been a remarkable example of self-reliance over the years. She said this while releasing the 7th Edition of the National Formulary of India in New Delhi. The Minister said that currently more than one thousand one hundred Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring Centres are operational in the country and the Government aims to increase this number up to the primary health facility level.She also said that 25 countries in the world recognise and accept the Indian pharmacopoeia and added that the country now provides pharmacovigilance data to the WHO patient safety database. The Minister highlighted that India has risen from the 123rd rank in 2014 to the 8th rank in providing this data to WHO. India achieved this milestone in the year 2025. On the occasion, the Minister appealed to the citizens to avoid any form of self-medication, follow professional prescriptions, and never ignore a sudden or unexpected side effect of any medicinal drug.

. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Suchika Tariyal on creating history by winning the Bronze Medal in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) at the Asian Games 2026, being held in Nagoya, Japan. In a social media post, the President said that this achievement holds special significance for Indian sport, as it marks the debut of MMA at the Games.President Murmu has also congratulated Himanshu Dhillon on winning the Silver Medal in the Men’s 10m Air Rifle Individual Final and Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil on securing the Bronze Medal in the Men’s 10m Air Rifle Individual event at the Games. She said that their impressive performance reflects focus, dedication and sporting excellence. She wished them continued success and many more accomplishments in the years ahead.

. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri met a delegation of Japanese Parliamentarians from the Liberal Democratic Party in New Delhi. The delegation is being led by Director General of LDP’s International Bureau, Taro Kono, who has previously served as Japan’s Defence Minister, Foreign Minister and Digital Minister. The delegation is on a five-day visit to India under the India-Japan Distinguished Visitors Programme.The External Affairs Ministry said in a statement that both sides held productive discussions on continuing the positive momentum in bilateral ties across a host of domains. These include defence, economic security, supply chain resilience, trade and investment, technology, innovation and people-to-people linkages. The visiting delegation noted the impressive strides made by the Indian deep-tech entrepreneurship and research and innovation ecosystem. They made a positive mention of the scope and speed of India’s economic development, including its manufacturing heft and the opportunities it is generating for India and its partner countries. They assessed the need for a more intensive economic security partnership between India and Japan, with an objective to further strengthen de-risking and supply chain resilience.Both sides underlined the importance of the India-Japan Special Strategic and Global Partnership built on the foundations of political trust, mutual goodwill and a common strategic outlook as an anchor for peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific. They appreciated the need to move quickly to enhance the scope and depth of India-Japan engagement guided by the directions set by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi during the 16th Annual Summit.

. The International Day of Sign Languages is being observed today to raise awareness about the importance of sign languages in ensuring the human rights of Deaf people.The theme this year is “Declaring Deaf People’s Human Rights.” According to the United Nations, the theme calls for making the rights of Deaf people a reality in all areas of life, with a focus on access through national sign languages. The day is especially significant this year as it marks the 75th anniversary of the World Federation of the Deaf and 20 years since the adoption of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.The World Federation of the Deaf is also observing the International Week of Deaf People till 27th of September, with a focus on inclusive education, accessibility, Deaf culture and participation. The UN General Assembly declared September 23 as the International Day of Sign Languages in 2017.

. The first V4 + India Foreign Ministers’ Meeting was held on the margins of the Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York yesterday. External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar participated in the meeting along with Foreign Ministers of Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic. The meeting was held under the Slovak Presidency of the V4.The Ministers exchanged views on ways to strengthen engagement between India and the Visegrad Group. They acknowledged the strong bilateral relations that exist between India and each of the V4 countries, and noted the potential for the V4+India format to complement and add further momentum to these ties.External Affairs Ministry said that the discussions covered opportunities for cooperation in areas such as trade and investment, technology and innovation, resilient supply chains, defence and security, connectivity, education, mobility and people-to-people exchanges. The Ministers also discussed possibilities for greater interaction between businesses, academic and research institutions and other stakeholders from India and the V4 member states.The Ministers also exchanged perspectives on global and regional developments, peace and security, and cooperation in multilateral fora. Discussions included the need for reformed multilateralism and addressing contemporary global challenges, including those affecting the Global South.The Ministry stated that the inaugural meeting marked an important step in establishing engagement between India and the Visegrad Group at the Foreign Ministers’ level. The V4+India format offers an additional platform for dialogue and cooperation, building upon India’s longstanding and substantive relations with V4 countries.The V4+India group is a diplomatic dialogue format that brings together India and the Visegrád Group (V4)-comprising Central European nations Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, and the Czech Republic. The Visegrad Group (V4) is a cultural and political alliance that aims to advance cooperation in military, economic, cultural, and energy affairs.

. The Government today clarified that GST on UPI Merchant Discount Rate, or MDR, will not burden small merchants or make digital payments expensive. In a social media post, National Payments Corporation of India  (NPCI) has termed such media reports as incorrect. It said, MDR applies only to person-to-merchant transactions above two thousand rupees. It said person-to-merchant transactions up to two thousand rupees continue to have zero MDR and therefore zero GST impact. NPCI stated that transactions of up to two thousand rupees constitute more than 96 per cent of UPI merchant transaction volume. The GST paid on MDR by a merchant will be adjusted against the GST payable on the sale of goods, in the same manner that input taxes are set off against output tax liability. NPCI said that merchants with monthly UPI receipts of up to one lakh rupees are not liable to pay MDR.

. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres pleaded for a world built on interdependence as he made his final address today to the General Assembly gathering of world leaders. The UN leader has long implored leaders not to give up on cooperation and shared decision-making in the face of accelerating global challenges and increasing great-powers competition. He urged world leaders to regulate artificial intelligence, end wars, focus on climate change and overhaul UN institutions which are struggling to confront mounting global challenges. Today’s message took on additional urgency because Guterres leaves office at the end of this year. His speech opened the main portion of the world’s biggest diplomatic meeting of the year. Leaders from the UN’s 193 member countries address each other and the international community and air their hopes, plans and grievances. The annual high-level gathering at the UN General Assembly will be consumed with wars in Iran, Gaza, Ukraine, Sudan, Congo and Myanmar and a persisting question: Can the leaders do anything to end them?

. President Droupadi Murmu will grace the 75th annual convocation ceremony of the Maharaja Sayajirao University at Vadodara today.  She will also launch Brahma Kumaris’ campaign and inaugurate the ‘Global Spiritual Palace’ at Vadodara.In the 75th convocation ceremony, President Murmu will confer degrees to over 12,600 students. This includes 6,713 from the Faculty of Commerce and 1,012 from the Faculty of Technology and Engineering. During the ceremony, a total of 201 gold medals will be awarded to 160 students for their academic achievements in undergraduate and postgraduate courses.After that, the President will inaugurate the Global Spiritual Palace Retreat Centre of Brahma Kumaris in Vadodara. During the programme, the President will also inaugurate the “Spiritual Awakening for World Renewal” project and will virtually launch the ‘Youth for Viksit Bharat: Awakening Inner Strength for Nation Building’ campaign. Gujarat Governor Acharya Devvrat and Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel will be present on the occasion.

. National Human Rights Commission Chairperson, Justice V. Ramasubramanian has emphasised the need for greater collaboration among National Commissions to promote and protect human rights. He made the remarks while addressing a Statutory Full Commission meeting with representatives of the seven deemed members of the NHRC in New Delhi yesterday.Justice Ramasubramanian said, by working together, the Commissions can undertake meaningful initiatives to promote and protect the rights of various sections of society. He suggested appointing a Nodal Officer to coordinate among all the National Commissions. He also said that the NHRC could explore extending support to other Commissions, particularly in areas where they lack adequate investigative resources.Justice Ramasubramanian expressed concern over the lack of rehabilitation measures for mentally ill women engaged in begging. He stressed the need to review policies concerning the welfare of persons with disabilities and identify existing gaps. He also raised concerns over inadequate social security for persons with disabilities and the denial of insurance coverage by insurance companies.The seven deemed members of the NHRC are the National Commissions for Women, for Backward Classes, for Protection of Child Rights, for Scheduled Castes, for Minorities, for Scheduled Tribes, and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities.National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) special rapporteur Sayeed Ahmed Baba addressed a meeting with heads of government departments at Saitual district in Mizoram yesterday. Mr Ahmad has stressed the need for greater public awareness of human rights and adequate counselling and de-addiction facilities for people, particularly youngsters, affected by substance abuse. He also stressed on the responsibility of government officials, whose work directly affects the lives and well-being of people, to ensure that their rights are respected and protected.

. US President Donald Trump has defended his administration’s military action against Iran in an address to the 81st UN General Assembly in New York yesterday. He urged countries to maintain economic pressure on Tehran and said Iran faces a choice between reaching a deal and facing further US military action.Mr Trump said the United States had targeted Iran’s nuclear programme and weakened its military capabilities. He reiterated that Washington would not allow Iran to acquire nuclear weapons. He also called for the complete economic isolation of Iran until it ends attacks on commercial shipping and its support for what he described as terrorism.On other foreign policy issues, Mr Trump said efforts were continuing to end the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Mr. Trump highlighted a series of developments across the Western Hemisphere, including what he described as a US military operation in Venezuela that resulted in the arrest of President Nicolás Maduro. He said the US was now working with Venezuelan leaders toward what he called “a much better future for the Venezuelan people” and announced a major oil agreement between the two countries.On Mexico, the President focused on efforts against transnational crime, saying drug cartels had been designated as foreign terrorist organisations and calling on the country to reclaim control of its soil from the enemies of humanity. He also cited ongoing negotiations with Cuba, saying his administration sought a fundamental change in the situation there.The President also lauded the new agreement due to be signed with Greenland, describing the Arctic territory as strategically important to regional and international security. Mr. Trump said the arrangement with Denmark and Greenland would give the United States “permanent control over security and all other needs” on the territory and would support NATO’s security posture in the Arctic and North Atlantic regions.A significant portion of the address also focused on artificial intelligence (AI). He said the United States would promote the development of artificial intelligence, which he called “superintelligence”, while rejecting what he described as international attempts to control the technology.He also criticised several international bodies including the International Criminal Court, UNESCO and the UN Human Rights Council. Mr. Trump described the International Criminal Court (ICC) as an institution full of evil people with no jurisdiction over the United States and called on nations to withdraw from it.The President was similarly critical of the Geneva-based UN Human Rights Council, accusing it of focusing excessively on the US while overlooking abuses elsewhere. He criticised the education, culture and science agency, UNESCO and the International Maritime Organization, arguing that international bodies should not advance what he characterised as global governance initiatives.

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. Indian men’s Badminton team produced a superlative performance to outwit hosts Japan in the quarterfinals and assure itself of a medal at the Asian Games at Nagoya, Japan, today. Lakshya Sen was staring at defeat after losing the opening game and trailing 14-19 in the decider. However, Lakshya made a comeback, reeling off seven straight points to beat world No.7 and two-time world championships silver-medallist Kodai Naraoka 11-21, 21-5, 21-19 to give India a 1-0 lead. Playing the first doubles, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, who have won two titles this season, registered a 21-18, 24-22 win over former world champions Hoki Takuro and Kobayashi Yugo to extend India’s lead to 2-0. Ayush Shetty then produced an impressive performance to see off world no. 16 Koki Watanabe 21-10, 21-19 to seal the match and a medal for India.India will face the winner of the other quarterfinal between defending champions China and Korea in the last four stage tomorrow. The Indian men were the silver medalists of the last edition.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said its special US dollar-Indian rupee (USD-INR) forex swap facility has received forex inflows of over 143.5 billion US dollars till September 18, 2026. According to the latest data, Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) [FCNR-B] deposits accounted for the overwhelming majority, amounting to 132.98 billion US dollars. Meanwhile, Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCBs) brought in 5.32 billion US dollars and External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) contributed 5.29 billion US dollars. The Apex Bank introduced the special USD-INR forex swap facility covering FCNR(B) deposits, ECBs and OFCBs inflows on June 8, 2026, to boost the inflow of dollars amid a weakening rupee. The FCNR(B) deposits scheme was closed on August 31, 2026, while the facility for ECBs and OFCBs remains available until December 31, 2026

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended 0.4 per cent lower today. The Sensex lost 330 points to close at 74,529. The Nifty dropped 85 points to settle at 23,329.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Nifty Midcap 100 index dipped 0.1 per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 index declined 0.2 per cent.In the forex market, the rupee depreciated by 22 paise to trade at 95 rupees and 59 paise against the US dollar.In the global crude oil market, Brent Crude was trading 2.6 per cent down at 97 US dollars and 71 cents per barrel, while WTI Crude was trading 3.1 per cent lower at 92 US dollars and 78 cents per barrel in intra-day trade.At the Multi Commodity Exchange, Gold for the October contract was trading 0.4 per cent down at 1,52,511 rupees per 10 grams, and Silver for the December contract was trading half a per cent lower at 2,38,130 rupees per kilogram, when reports last came in.For more updates about the market activities, tune in to Akashvani’s bilingual programme ‘Market Mantra’ at 6:30 PM this evening.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Sri Sri Vishwaprasanna Tirtha Swamiji of Sri Pejavara Adhokshaja Matha, Udupi, along with other dignitaries in New Delhitoday. On the occasion, Mr Modi unveiled the logo of the Birth Centenary Celebrations of Padma Vibhushan Yatikula Chakravarti Sri Vishwesha Tirtha Swamiji. In a social media post, Mr Modi said, the life of devotion, learning and service of Sri Vishwesha Tirtha Swami continues to inspire countless people. He said, the various initiatives being undertaken in the run-up to his birth centenary will further carry forward his noble ideals.

. World Rhino Day is being observed today across the world, including India, to raise awareness about protecting the five remaining rhinoceros species.This year’s theme, “Keep the Five Alive,” calls for stronger efforts to protect rhino habitats, prevent poaching and curb the illegal trade in rhino horn. Only around 27-thousand rhinos remain in the wild, compared with nearly five lakh a century ago.India is home to the greater one-horned rhinoceros, whose population has recovered to nearly four thousand in India and Nepal, from around 200, following sustained conservation efforts.A programme is being organised today at Neelpara Ground in Alipurduar to mark this day.

. In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

. India has reaffirmed its commitment to combating Viral Hepatitis and eliminating Hepatitis B and C as public health threats by 2030. Addressing a side event of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, organised by the UN Group of Friends to Eliminate Hepatitis, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava highlighted India’s comprehensive, people-centred response across prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment and care.The Health Secretary said India has strengthened interventions across the continuum from antenatal screening and Hepatitis B immunisation to free diagnosis and treatment, safe blood transfusion services, counselling and rehabilitation support for people who inject drugs. She emphasised the importance of sustained global cooperation, equitable access to prevention, testing and treatment, and stronger health systems to accelerate progress towards the 2030 targets.

. The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

. Union Minister of New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi has congratulated Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) on its 15th Foundation Day today. In a social media post, Mr Joshi said that SECI has played an important role in advancing India’s renewable energy journey and strengthening the country’s clean energy ecosystem over the past 15 years.
